title: Hubble view of the surroundings of a hidden neutron star in the Small Magellanic Cloud
caption: The supernova remnant 1E 0102.2-7219 in the Small Magellanic Cloud, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
credit: NASA, ESA and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Blue wisps of gas near the centre of this Hubble image form the supernova remnant 1E 0102.2-7219, while part of N 76 (also called Henize 1956), a massive star-forming region, glows green and pink at lower right. The scene lies in the Small Magellanic Cloud, one of our nearest neighbouring galaxies.

A supernova remnant is the expanding cloud of debris left behind when a massive star explodes. This picture sets the scene for a search for an elusive missing object hidden in a complex tangle of gaseous filaments: a neutron star, the ultra-dense collapsed core that such an explosion can leave behind.

Finding such a remnant core is difficult, because a neutron star is tiny and faint compared with the glowing gas around it. Hubble's wide range of filters, from ultraviolet to near-infrared, helps separate the different gases in the scene.

understand.summary: This image combines many filters from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys and Wide Field Camera 3, from ultraviolet to near-infrared, including ones that isolate glowing oxygen, hydrogen and sulphur. The remnant's gas appears blue, but the full colour mapping isn't published.
filters: 665 nm · Optical Redshifted H-Alpha + NII (Hubble WFC3)
understand.eye: Several of these filters capture ultraviolet or near-infrared light the eye cannot see, and narrow filters isolate the glow of particular gases.

explore: The Small Magellanic Cloud lies in the direction of the constellation Tucana. This image draws on two Hubble cameras, the Advanced Camera for Surveys and Wide Field Camera 3, and on many filters that isolate light from specific elements such as oxygen, hydrogen, nitrogen and sulphur.
alt: Blue wisps of gas near the centre and a green and pink star-forming region at lower right.
